chunks: And the Shaykh — may God the Exalted support him — informed me, saying: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him)

He said: I asked him about nosebleed (ru'af), cupping (hijama), and every flowing blood. He said: 'There is no wudu (required) for this. Indeed, wudu is only from your two ends with which God has blessed you.'

key_terms.الرُّعَافِ: nosebleed (ru'af); blood from the nose, ruled not to nullify wudu in Shia fiqh
key_terms.الْحِجَامَةِ: cupping (hijama); therapeutic bloodletting, similarly not a nullifier of wudu
key_terms.طَرَفَيْكَ: your two ends; euphemism for the two lower orifices (urinary and anal), the actual obligatory sources of wudu
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: wudu; ritual ablution prerequisite for salat, here used to mean its obligation is triggered

ai.seo_question: Does nosebleed or cupping (hijama) nullify wudu according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Abu Basir asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether nosebleed, cupping (hijama), and all flowing blood require wudu. The Imam ruled that they do not; wudu is necessitated only by what issues from 'your two ends' — a Shia jurisprudential idiom for the anterior and posterior orifices. This hadith establishes the Shia fiqh position, contrary to certain Sunni schools, that blood exiting the body does not invalidate ritual purity.
